Subject: QBR prep - stability sentinel & contingency asks

Team / Raj,

As we prep the QBR packet for Acorn Health and the broader Q1 review, I want to call out the operating risks that need clear owners and contingency decisions. Attached: qbr_risk_registry_2027_v1.xlsx and timeline_v2.pdf — please update row ownerships in the registry by EOD Monday.

Priority asks: 
- Engineering: short summary (2 bullets) of current blockers that could shift SLA exposure, plus an ETA for mitigation and whether a canary rollback path exists.
- Product: identify any features scheduled for the Q2 cut that are non-blocking for the commercial rollout and propose which can slip to reduce risk.
- Leadership: two decision points for go/no-go + proposed thresholds (latency, error rate, infra headroom).

For context, Acorn wants confirmation by the week of Apr 4. Raj — we included your current list of telemetry asks; if anything changed, flag it here.

Attachments: qbr_risk_registry_2027_v1.xlsx (xlsx), timeline_v2.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Irene Choi

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep - stability sentinel & contingency asks

Irene — quick engineering readout below. I kept it tight so we can paste into the packet.

- Blocker: KV cache pressure under long context workloads. Repro in staging when sequences > 8k with concurrent streams > 120. Impact: intermittent latency spikes (~300-400ms tail) that could affect the 99th percentile.
  - Mitigation in flight: memory tuning (rolling config) and a hotfix that reduces retention window — patch ready, QA tomorrow.
  - Contingency: enable prefix-only caching and move affected customers to a dedicated smaller pool; fallback to a slightly larger model quantization profile temporarily.
  - ETA: rolling hotfix + canary by Mar 31; full rollback path exists (toggle in runtime).

- Blocker: KV cache eviction race during burst autoscale. Impact: rare token duplication and invalidation errors (observed 1.2% of bursts).
  - Mitigation: conservative autoscale thresholds; we have an infra patch (perf_patch.diff) that reduces race window.
  - ETA: deploy to canary Apr 1; full rollout Apr 6 if no regressions.

Operational asks from Eng: 
1) Approve temporary dedicated pool option for Acorn (cost caveat) so we can avoid cross-tenant tail latencies during their heavy inference windows.
2) Confirm that Product is comfortable sliding non-critical visualization work off the Apr cut to minimize churn during rollouts.

Attaching perf_patch.diff for review.

- Karthik
Engineering Director, Serving Runtime

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep - stability sentinel & contingency asks

Thanks Karthik — added a short product section below that I can paste into the QBR slide and the packet.

Product readiness snapshot (Apr 4 target):
- Core inference UX (APIs, streaming, function-calling): 88% (tests passing in staging; a small telemetry schema break requires a quick adapter).
- Analytics dashboard (per-route cost/latency): 45% — this was scoped as a stretch for Apr and I propose we deprioritize until after the commercial SLA baseline is stable.
- Canary plans: we need 4 business days of telemetry post-canary to validate tail regressions.

Risks and recommended trade-offs: 
- Risk: pushing analytics features in the same window as the KV hotfix increases blast radius.
  - Recommendation: delay analytics dashboard non-blocking items to May.
- Risk: customer communications — Acorn needs transparency on what to expect during canary (latency variance + potential short maintenance windows).
  - Recommendation: provide a short runbook and a <48h notice for any rolling deploys.

If leadership approves the dedicated pool ask (see Karthik), product will own the customer comms and the conditioned rollout plan.

- Grace
VP Product, Serving Platform

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Raj Mehta <raj@acornhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep - stability sentinel & contingency asks

High level — good, and thanks for the crisp asks. Two quick leadership-level decisions we need to surface in the QBR and commit to: 

1) Approve the temporary dedicated pool for Acorn (cost vs SLA trade). If approved, Finance needs an estimate and CS needs to prep comms.
2) Formalize go/no-go thresholds: 99th latency < 350ms, production error rate < 0.5% sustained over a 72h window post-canary. If we miss these, we pause and roll back.

Operational timeline for the board:
- Mar 31: engineering canary deploy (if QA passes).
- Apr 4-7: telemetry window and customer validation (4 business days).
- Apr 8: go/no-go decision (leadership sync).

Irene — please assemble the mutual action plan with owners (product, eng, cs, finance) and include the cost delta for the dedicated pool. Put that doc into the Drive link and send Raj the runbook excerpt so he's not surprised.

- Vivek
SVP, Product & Ops

- Grace: draft customer runbook & comms; confirm which analytics items slip to May (due: 2027-04-01).
- Tessa: update the mutual action plan with milestones and attach cost estimate for dedicated pool (due: 2027-04-01).

Decision pending: approval of dedicated pool for Acorn (Finance estimate required). If approved, we proceed with canary Mar 31 and hold telemetry window Apr 4-7. If not approved, we will trigger the fallback path (prefix-only cache + quantization profile).
